Strokes: a straight rim (12865, 881) -> (12897, 881) with dark inner shading; its sides converge to a narrow bottom at about (12880-12888, 915-920). A frame of thin posts and two rails stands just east of it at u 12895-12932, v 907-952, either the railing's east bay where the raised floor ends (u ~12930) or the vessel's stand. READING 2: it stands on a tall stand of its own on the ground beside the seated man (S4b.fig.man_seated_front_of_hall_12866, foot est v ~990): base est (12884, 990), support 'ground', a stand about as tall as the seated man. lessons: Compare the restyle with the overlay side by side (overlay | restyle) at zoom 1.8-3 in every dense window, not only the scan with the overlay. On S4b's west half this found a slatted crate and a funnel-shaped vessel that the restyle painted and no unit recorded. Read each one on the scan before proposing it: the restyle names a faded thing, and the strokes place it.

A head drawn across a lintel or an eave line is suspect. Inside a hall the lintel hides anything above it, and a figure in front of the posts would show its body below. On S4b two 'dim heads' sat on the official hall's lintel; one was the same blob that the structures agent called a hanging lamp, and the restyle painted both as hanging things.
Count the legs under furniture. Five legs under one table's west end mean a second piece: on S4b a bench was read as a counter's west side.
